facts.ALS-U Status: This beamline will temporarily close during the ALS-U dark time and will resume operations after a commissioning period. For more information, see ALS-U Beamline Impacts and ALS-U Timeline and Facility Impacts .
facts.Research areas: Applied Sciences Biological Sciences Chemical Sciences Energy Sciences Earth & Environmental Sciences Materials Sciences Physical Sciences
facts.Technique category: Spectroscopy X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy (XFS) Scattering/Diffraction Coherent scattering Small-angle x-ray scattering (SAXS) Wide-angle x-ray scattering (WAXS) Grazing-incidence SAXS/WAXS Magnetic scattering Resonant scattering
facts.Additional notes: Polarization is user selectable; linear polarization continuously variable from horizontal to vertical; left and right elliptical (or circular) polarization. Spot size = 100 μm diameter. Field of view/spatial resolution = down to 2 nm resolution. Sample information: Polymer thin films, solid thin films, vacuum compatible liquid cell. Other notes: High vacuum, heating.

header.Drawing: BL 11.0.1.2 RSOXS · Reflectometer endstation · device blueprint
header.sources: Scale none · schematic Ranges, units, gains bl11012/lv-config (read at build time) Meaning bl11012/bl11012_knowledge.md Parts A–B, through bl11012/mapping (read at build time) Geometry kickoff deck slides 5–6 · review with Thomas, 2026-09-09 Beam ~200–1500 eV · ~10¹³ ph/s · E/ΔE 4000 at 800 eV · 400 × 300 µm History A 2026-09-05 draft · B 2026-09-08 door viewpoint · C 2026-09-08 team reference · D 2026-09-09 reviewed with Thomas Ferron · E 2026-09-09 interactive: tooltips, deep links, rules, photo

beam_stop_x.name: Beam Stop X
beam_stop_x.meaning: Physically mounted to the camera, so it moves with the camera (from the beam stop's frame nothing moves; the beam moves). Same axis as CCD X — to keep the beam covered, move the beam stop the same distance in the *opposite* direction as the detector (detect…

beamline_energy.name: Beamline Energy
beamline_energy.meaning: The number normally scanned. Setting it drives, via a LabVIEW lookup table, the EPU configuration (gap + Z offset) and the monochromator (two mirrors / two angles) synchronously. The gap/EPU-Z calculations are handled on a separate beamline computer, not th…

beamline_energy_goal.name: Beamline Energy Goal
beamline_energy_goal.meaning: The requested energy as LabVIEW records it; the only energy entry flagged Motor Used? = true.

camera_roi_height.name: Camera ROI Height
camera_roi_height.meaning: Region-of-interest height; the sensor reads row by row, so a shorter ROI is a faster frame.

camera_roi_x.name: Camera ROI X
camera_roi_x.meaning: Region-of-interest X offset of the camera, exposed as a LabVIEW variable.

camera_temp_setpoint.name: Camera Temp Setpoint
camera_temp_setpoint.meaning: Camera cooler setpoint exposed as a LabVIEW variable (CCD Positions tab).

ccd_camera_shutter_inhibit.name: CCD Camera Shutter Inhibit
ccd_camera_shutter_inhibit.meaning: The camera-side view of the Shutter Inhibit flag (A.12) exposed as a LabVIEW variable.

ccd_shutter_control.name: CCD Shutter Control
ccd_shutter_control.meaning: Camera "Shutter Options" setting from the CCD Positions tab; not discussed (to verify).

ccd_theta.name: CCD Theta
ccd_theta.meaning: Rotates the entire detector in an arc around a point that should be the sample rotation axis (but isn't exactly). As theta rotates, the beam drifts across the detector in an arc. There is no CCD Z — the arc plays that role, which is what you want in a scatt…

ccd_x.name: CCD X
ccd_x.meaning: In/out from the beam. Moving it makes the beam move across the detector face.

ccd_y.name: CCD Y
ccd_y.meaning: Brings the detector closer to / farther from the sample — changes the scattering vector observed. Closer in = higher angles; farther out = shallower angles. CCD Y = 80 is the safe, fully-out position (see Collision hazards).

coolstage.name: Coolstage
coolstage.meaning: Setpoint of the manual cool-stage cube, exposed as a LabVIEW motor. Out of scope; interlocks involved.

diag_106.name: Diag 106
diag_106.meaning: The 106 diagnostic paddle, which carries the I0 gold mesh. Moved in to a preset position (stored on the other computer) when the diagnostic is wanted — done about once in 10 years.

entrance_slit_width.name: Entrance Slit width
entrance_slit_width.meaning: Width of the monochromator entrance slit, set in microns during the radiation-shielding setup and then left alone; the second entry in eV is probably an old leftover (Thomas, 2026-09-09).

entrance_slit_width_2.name: Entrance Slit Width
entrance_slit_width_2.meaning: Width of the monochromator entrance slit, set in microns during the radiation-shielding setup and then left alone; the second entry in eV is probably an old leftover (Thomas, 2026-09-09).

epu_gap.name: EPU Gap
epu_gap.meaning: Undulator gap; sets the photon energy. Driven indirectly through the Beamline Energy lookup table, not moved by hand (inferred from the transcript).

epu_polarization.name: EPU Polarization
epu_polarization.meaning: Undulator (Elliptically Polarizing Undulator) polarization setting; a value like 100 corresponds to a specific EPU gap and magnet-row Z offset. In practice they pick 100 or 190. (Shifting the magnet rows turns in-plane polarization into circular polarization.)

epu_z.name: EPU Z
epu_z.meaning: Magnet-row longitudinal offset; sets the polarization. Driven indirectly through the EPU Polarization setting (100 or 190).

exit_slit_bottom.name: Exit Slit Bottom
exit_slit_bottom.meaning: The other blade of the vertical exit slit (inferred).

exit_slit_left.name: Exit Slit Left
exit_slit_left.meaning: One blade of the horizontal exit slit (inferred).

exit_slit_right.name: Exit Slit Right
exit_slit_right.meaning: The other blade of the horizontal exit slit (inferred).

exit_slit_top.name: Exit Slit Top
exit_slit_top.meaning: One blade of the vertical exit slit; normally driven through Size/Position, not directly (inferred).

higher_order_suppressor.name: Higher Order Suppressor
higher_order_suppressor.meaning: Should roughly linearly attenuate the beam as it goes up. Used for reflectivity; moved a lot during operation, but not critical for the current automation target.

horizontal_exit_slit_position.name: Horizontal Exit Slit Position
horizontal_exit_slit_position.meaning: Translates both horizontal blades together (LabVIEW combines the two blade motors). Displayed microns are not physical.

horizontal_exit_slit_size.name: Horizontal Exit Slit Size
horizontal_exit_slit_size.meaning: Opens/closes the horizontal blades symmetrically. Displayed microns are not physical.

horizontal_slit_position.name: Horizontal Slit Position
horizontal_slit_position.meaning: Exit-slit axis after M103 (Thomas, 2026-09-09); relation to Horizontal Exit Slit Position to clarify.

horizontal_slit_size.name: Horizontal Slit Size
horizontal_slit_size.meaning: Exit-slit axis after M103 (Thomas, 2026-09-09); relation to Horizontal Exit Slit Size to clarify.

in_chamber_jj_horz_aperture.name: In-Chamber JJ Horz Aperture
in_chamber_jj_horz_aperture.meaning: Horizontal opening of the in-chamber slit set.

in_chamber_jj_horz_trans.name: In-Chamber JJ Horz Trans
in_chamber_jj_horz_trans.meaning: Horizontal position of the in-chamber slit set.

in_chamber_jj_vert_aperture.name: In-Chamber JJ Vert Aperture
in_chamber_jj_vert_aperture.meaning: Vertical opening of the last slit set, inside the chamber just before the sample.

in_chamber_jj_vert_trans.name: In-Chamber JJ Vert Trans
in_chamber_jj_vert_trans.meaning: Vertical position of the in-chamber slit set.

m101_feedback.name: M101 Feedback
m101_feedback.meaning: Does not exist as hardware: an attempt at mirror feedback about 25 years ago that never worked and was never touched since; a leftover entry in the export (Thomas, 2026-09-09).

m101_horizontal_deflection.name: M101 Horizontal Deflection
m101_horizontal_deflection.meaning: Horizontal tilt of the first mirror; jogged together with the vertical one.

m101_vertical_deflection.name: M101 Vertical Deflection
m101_vertical_deflection.meaning: Vertical tilt of the first mirror; jogged by hand to recover intensity when the mount drifts.

m103_bend_down.name: M103 Bend Down
m103_bend_down.meaning: Bends the other KB mirror; moves the focal point. Driven to encoded presets.

m103_bend_up.name: M103 Bend Up
m103_bend_up.meaning: Bends one KB mirror; moves the focal point. Driven to encoded presets.

m103_yaw.name: M103 Yaw
m103_yaw.meaning: Yaw of the KB pair; a physical position that moves the beam. Driven to encoded presets.

m121_translation.name: M121 Translation
m121_translation.meaning: The vertical deflecting mirror that sends the beam to this endstation: two positions only — all the way up (in the beam) or all the way down (out). A physical catch/hard stop blocks motion beyond the useful position, so the procedure is simply "drive until…

middle_jj_horz_aperture.name: Middle JJ Horz Aperture
middle_jj_horz_aperture.meaning: Horizontal opening of the middle slit set.

middle_jj_horz_trans.name: Middle JJ Horz Trans
middle_jj_horz_trans.meaning: Horizontal position of the middle slit set.

middle_jj_vert_aperture.name: Middle JJ Vert Aperture
middle_jj_vert_aperture.meaning: Vertical opening of the middle slit set.

middle_jj_vert_trans.name: Middle JJ Vert Trans
middle_jj_vert_trans.meaning: Vertical position of the middle slit set.

mono_101_grating.name: Mono 101 Grating
mono_101_grating.meaning: Grating-side axis of the monochromator; moved by the energy lookup, not by hand (inferred; not discussed in the meeting).

mono_101_vessel.name: Mono 101 Vessel
mono_101_vessel.meaning: Drop-down of LabVIEW "preset positions" (250, 500, or 1000 lines/mm). The mono is one mirror with three line gratings; this moves the Mono 101 Vessel motor to a preset position (≈ −22) to pick the grating. Changed maybe once or twice a day — the beam shifts…

mono_energy.name: Mono Energy
mono_energy.meaning: The monochromator's own energy readback/setpoint, one of the three energy records in the export; which one a scan actually drives is an open question (C.8).

piezoshutter_trans.name: PiezoShutter Trans
piezoshutter_trans.meaning: Translation of the old PZT shutter — not used by this endstation anymore, but the PEEM instrument still uses it. A stored position is sent to move it out of the way; worth checking it's out when switching to this instrument. Don't touch otherwise.

sample_theta.name: Sample Theta
sample_theta.meaning: Rotation stage carrying the sample X–Y cross.

sample_x.name: Sample X
sample_x.meaning: Left/right relative to the beam (beam coming at you): in/out from the back of the chamber. This definition is always the same. Not encoded — position drifts slightly.

sample_y.name: Sample Y
sample_y.meaning: Coupled to Z and Theta (see below).

sample_z.name: Sample Z
sample_z.meaning: Coupled to Y and Theta (see below).

t_2t.name: T-2T
t_2t.meaning: Derived θ–2θ axis: moves sample theta and detector theta together (sample at 5° puts the detector at 10°) so the reflected beam stays on the detector. The two rotation axes are not coaxial, which is what the Set Theta–2Theta Detector Offset corrects. Legacy…

temperature_controller.name: Temperature Controller
temperature_controller.meaning: Setpoint of the external Peltier temperature controller, exposed as a LabVIEW motor. Out of scope for the current automation.

upstream_jj_horz_aperture.name: Upstream JJ Horz Aperture
upstream_jj_horz_aperture.meaning: Horizontal opening of the first slit set.

upstream_jj_horz_trans.name: Upstream JJ Horz Trans
upstream_jj_horz_trans.meaning: Horizontal position of the first slit set.

upstream_jj_vert_aperture.name: Upstream JJ Vert Aperture
upstream_jj_vert_aperture.meaning: Vertical opening of the first slit set, right after the gold mesh; two blades move symmetrically. Sets the approximate beam size.

upstream_jj_vert_trans.name: Upstream JJ Vert Trans
upstream_jj_vert_trans.meaning: Vertical position of the first slit set; both blades move together.

vertical_exit_slit_size.name: Vertical Exit Slit Size
vertical_exit_slit_size.meaning: Opens/closes the vertical blades symmetrically; the critical one for resolution. A displayed 62 is really about 25 µm.

vertical_slit_position.name: Vertical Slit Position
vertical_slit_position.meaning: Exit-slit axis "after the 103" per Thomas (2026-09-09); how it relates to Vertical Exit Slit Position above is still to clarify.

vertical_slit_size.name: Vertical Slit Size
vertical_slit_size.meaning: Exit-slit axis after M103 (Thomas, 2026-09-09); relation to Vertical Exit Slit Size to clarify.

ai_0.name: AI 0
ai_0.meaning: Traced recently; believed connected to nothing. Reserved for future use.

ai_3_izero.name: AI 3 Izero
ai_3_izero.meaning: A gold-coated copper mesh before all the beam-shaping slits, permanently in the beam. Continuously measures drain current (a TEY-type signal off gold), cutting ~10% of the beam. This is the intensity-vs-time monitor and the normalization signal for all meas…

ai_5.name: AI 5
ai_5.meaning: Believed to no longer exist / nothing.

ai_6_beamstop.name: AI 6 BeamStop
ai_6_beamstop.meaning: Being installed next cycle: a literal photodiode replacing the current silicon beam stop in front of the area detector. Will measure the flux through the sample, enabling absorption measurement *simultaneously* with scattering. Will always be recorded once…

ai_7.name: AI 7
ai_7.meaning: Unknown; Tom wants to trace it to confirm it isn't connected anywhere.

beam_current.name: Beam Current
beam_current.meaning: Literally the storage-ring beam current. Reads 0 when the beam is down.

camera_temp_setpoint_ai.name: Camera Temp Setpoint
camera_temp_setpoint_ai.meaning: Derived element (State Variable to AI): the camera cooler setpoint logged as a pseudo-AI.

ccd_temperature.name: CCD Temperature
ccd_temperature.meaning: Derived element: a LabVIEW number exposed as a pseudo-AI so it gets logged. The physical detector temperature readback (the ~16 °C on the controller) is currently represented nowhere in LabVIEW.

coolstage_temp_c.name: Coolstage Temp C
coolstage_temp_c.meaning: Derived element (Motor to AI): the cool-stage setpoint logged as a pseudo-AI.

deriv_photodiode.name: Deriv Photodiode
deriv_photodiode.meaning: Calculated AI: the derivative of the Photodiode signal.

epu_polarization_ai.name: EPU Polarization
epu_polarization_ai.meaning: Derived element (Motor to AI): the EPU Polarization setting (A.4) logged as a pseudo-AI.

izero.name: Izero
izero.meaning: Gold mesh monitor upstream of the end station, on the diagnostic paddle (see Diag 106 motor). It sits right after the M121 mirror (the mirror that redirects light to this chamber). Usually out of the beam, brought in by an old motor when needed — so it norm…

lv_memory.name: LV Memory
lv_memory.meaning: LabVIEW memory usage logged as a pseudo-AI.

pause_trigger.name: Pause Trigger
pause_trigger.meaning: NI DAQmx pulse output exposed as an AI; purpose unknown.

photodiode.name: Photodiode
photodiode.meaning: The primary, specifically calibrated photodiode. Located after the sample, physically attached to the side of the area detector. To use it, the camera is moved out of the way (beam onto the diode); camera comes back in for scattering. Used constantly, every…

temperature_controller_ai.name: Temperature Controller
temperature_controller_ai.meaning: Derived element (Motor to AI): the temperature-controller setpoint logged as a pseudo-AI.

tey_signal.name: TEY signal
tey_signal.meaning: Total Electron Yield: drain current from the sample bar. All samples sit on an aluminum plate that is electrically isolated from the chamber; a copper wire runs from the plate through a BNC feedthrough to a Keithley. Physics: X-rays eject electrons from the…

time_stamp_error.name: Time Stamp Error
time_stamp_error.meaning: State-variable pseudo-AI: timing error of the data time stamps.

time_stamp_server_time.name: Time Stamp Server Time
time_stamp_server_time.meaning: State-variable pseudo-AI: server time of the data time stamps.

time_stamp_transmit_time.name: Time Stamp Transmit Time

stages.name: Storage ring EPU M101 Mono 101 Exit slits M103 PZT shutter M121 Diag 106 Higher Order Suppressor Gold mesh Shutters Scatter slits (JJ) Sample stage Detector Beam stop Photodiode Ring lamp and video camera
stages.what: The ALS ring at 1.9 GeV ; electrons circulating in it make the X-rays. The undulator: two rows of magnets the electron beam wiggles through. The first mirror after the undulator. One mirror carrying three gratings (250, 500, 1000 lines/mm) that selects the photon energy. Two blade pairs at the focus of the upstream optics, downstream of M103 (Thomas, 2026-09-09); that focus is what gets imaged onto the sample. The Kirkpatrick–Baez focusing pair , between the mono and the exit slits (Thomas, 2026-09-09). The old piezo shutter , now used only by the PEEM instrument that shares the beamline. The vertical mirror that hands the beam to this endstation. A diagnostic paddle right after M121 carrying a spare gold-mesh I0. Grazing mirrors that strip the undulator's higher harmonics . A gold-coated copper mesh permanently in the beam before all the slits. A 2 ms fast shutter that times exposures, and one element downstream the old air shutter , kept as an emergency stop. Three sets (upstream, middle, in-chamber) of horizontal and vertical blade pairs ; JJ is the maker. A four-axis manipulator hanging from the back wall at pipe height: X slides the whole stack along the door axis, Y and Z form a cross on the rotation stage Θ , the sample bar bolts on top. The 2D camera ( AXIS-SXR-40 , bare sCMOS sensor) on an arc, a sideways slide and an in/out slide; the plate on top of its face (the forehead ) is the part that collides. A small block on the camera body in front of the sensor . The calibrated photodiode on the door side of the camera body (Thomas, 2026-09-09). A ring light and a video camera outside the vacuum , looking through a viewport at the top of the chamber right above the in-chamber slits, in the beam direction (Thomas, 2026-09-09).
stages.does: Beam Current is the ring current; Beam Dumped goes on when it falls below 10 mA. It is only logged : a scan that spans a dump is discarded and the optics realigned, no automatic resume (Thomas, 2026-09-09). The gap sets the photon energy, shifting the rows ( Z ) turns in-plane into circular polarization; operators pick polarization 100 or 190 and never move gap or Z by hand. Its mount drifts with heat, so the two deflections are jogged by hand during beamtime to recover intensity; no automation has worked. M101 Feedback does not exist (a 25-year-old attempt, Thomas 2026-09-09). Beamline Energy is the number scanned and the record a CCD Scan writes (a Beamline Scan writes Energy Goal instead, Thomas 2026-09-09): LabVIEW looks it up in a table and moves the EPU gap and the mono together; Mono 101 Vessel picks the grating and Energy Type (a state variable) picks the table, once or twice a day. Size opens the blades symmetrically, Position shifts both; the vertical size sets the resolution. The micron readouts are not physical (62 means about 25 µm). Yaw moves the beam, Bend Up / Bend Down move the focal point; set once per beamtime to encoded presets , no live optimisation. Its translation is sent to a stored position to park it out of the beam when this endstation takes over. Two positions only, in or out ; drive until the motor limit. The panel's To REFL button is this handover. Moved in about once a decade ; because it is normally out, its Izero signal reads nonsense. Moving it up attenuates the beam roughly linearly, which reflectivity uses to keep the detector in range. The beam knocks electrons out of the gold; the current flowing back ( AI 3 Izero ) is proportional to intensity, costs about 10 % of the beam, and normalises every measurement . Reads negative . They sit after the gold mesh, before the scatter slits (Thomas, 2026-09-09). The camera opens and closes the fast shutter around every exposure ; Shutter Inhibit (a software flag) stops it from opening, which is how a dark image is taken. Aperture moves a pair's two blades symmetrically to set the beam size, Trans moves both to set its position; aligned in order upstream → middle → in-chamber; hard limits, nothing can be damaged . All twelve read in mm (Thomas, 2026-09-09). X brings the bar into the beam (out below 8 mm); Θ turns the bar from grazing (0°) to normal incidence (90°); Y and Z swap between along-the-beam and up/down as Θ turns. TEY is the drain current from the isolated sample plate. CCD Θ swings the whole camera up through the scattering angles (−6° stop: the PEEM pass-through pipe; +122° stop: the in-chamber slits); CCD X moves it sideways (growing toward the back wall) so the spot lands elsewhere on the sensor, or at 90 puts the door-side photodiode in the beam; CCD Y sets the distance, hence the angles that fit on the sensor. CCD Y is motor counts between two hard stops, not a distance ; presets BS Center / BS Edge put the beam stop at the sensor centre or its edge (Thomas, 2026-09-09). Hides the direct beam , which would saturate the sensor; because it rides on the camera, a CCD X move needs the opposite Beam Stop X move to keep the beam covered. Its motors are the SmarAct X and Y axes, only Y in use and parked until its encoders are shielded (Thomas, 2026-09-09). Next cycle it becomes a photodiode ( AI 6 ). The everyday diagnostic : the Photodiode Far preset slides the camera aside along CCD X so the diode sits in the beam. The lamp lights the chamber so the camera can find the sample (YAG for the beam, crosshair for its position); it must be off during any exposure or the bare sensor records background and blobs. The detector cannot hit them.

rules.name: Before any acquisition Dark image Moving the detector Scanning energy Normalising Beam dump Signs and gains Finding the sample
rules.text: Before any acquisition Light Output off (the lamp puts background and blobs on the bare sensor), Air Shutter Output on (open), Shutter Inhibit off . The queueserver plans switch the light off themselves. Dark image Shutter Inhibit high , then count: the camera runs the exposure without ever opening the fast shutter. Moving the detector Out, then over : CCD Y → 80 first, then Sample X or CCD Θ, never a diagonal move. Large θ angles only at CCD Y = 80 . LabVIEW does not enforce this; the simulator refuses the move. Scanning energy Scan Beamline Energy (the record a CCD Scan writes). Never change Mono 101 Vessel or Energy Type during a scan: a grating change moves the beam and needs realignment. Normalising Divide every frame by the average of AI 3 Izero over its exposure; it is the only monitor that is always in the beam. Izero (the paddle) is normally out and reads nonsense. Beam dump Beam Dumped is only logged. A scan that spans a dump is discarded and the optics are realigned before continuing; no automatic resume. Signs and gains The real current channels read negative . Keithley gains (Photodiode 1 nA/V, Izero 10 nA/V, AI 3 1 nA/V, TEY 100 pA/V, AI 6 100 nA/V) are not yet remotely adjustable; LabVIEW auto-scales only the photodiode. Finding the sample Ring light on, video camera: the YAG shows the beam, the crosshair marks it; move Sample X in (nothing is in the beam below 8 mm) and Sample Y along the rows. Then light off.
